sector_model: insurance specialty P&C: judged on net income, return on equity, price to book, combined ratio, reserve development, reinsurance and catastrophe exposure; operating cash flow and enterprise value are not used as anchors
thesis: Palomar (Nasdaq: PLMR) is a specialty property and casualty insurer (earthquake, flood, crop, surety, casualty) growing quickly. Q3 2026 revenue 386.6M (+58% vs 244.7M); 9M revenue 980.0M vs 622.6M; Q3 gross written premiums 767.0M (+28.4%), 9M 2.0B (+32.0%), including the Gray Surety acquisition (2026-01-31, about 314.0M). GAAP net income Q3 65.3M (vs 51.5M); 9M 160.9M (vs 140.9M). Adjusted combined ratio 76.3% in Q3 (74.8% a year earlier). TTM to 2026-09-30 GAAP net income 217.0M (FY2025 197.1M minus 9M 2025 140.9M plus 9M 2026 160.9M). At the 2026-11-09 close of 156.78 and 26.29M shares (cover, 2026-11-04) market cap is about 4.12B: 19.0x TTM GAAP earnings and 4.2x book value (equity 985.0M at 2026-09-30); annualized 9M GAAP return on average equity about 22% (own calculation). Term loan debt 294.0M. The market appears to price a high growth, high ROE specialty insurer at a premium to book; the evidence that supports it is steady growth with a low combined ratio, while the price leaves little room for a reserve or catastrophe shock.
counterthesis: Growth is partly acquired and partly in crop and surety lines new to the story, so the 2025 earnings base is not like for like. Adjusted net income (9M 208.2M) exceeds GAAP (160.9M) by about 47M of excluded items, a gap the 10-Q reconciliation shows but this record did not decompose. Q3 had 4.0M of adverse prior year development (crop reallocation) against 20.6M favorable over nine months; catastrophe losses in Hawaii and Midwest floods; total liabilities rose from 2,108.3M to 3,184.3M in nine months, assets 3,051.0M to 4,169.2M, so leverage (liabilities to assets 76%) and reinsurance reliance rose; interest expense went from 0.3M to 13.2M for nine months on the term loan and an FHLB line. Other underwriting expenses +59.8%. At 4.2x book the stock depends on sustaining a very high ROE. The stock rose 8.8% in a week (144.04 on 11-04 to 156.78 on 11-09), so part of any discount to its recent range has closed.
invalidation: A combined ratio persistently above about 85%, material adverse reserve development, a large catastrophe loss exceeding reinsurance or reinsurance renewal on sharply worse terms, growth in crop or surety lines turning into underwriting losses, or ROE falling below about 15%.
